Subject: Post-call recap — appliance ownership, offline upgrades, next steps

Hey Elise / GenoQuip team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to get clarity on your compliance constraints and maintenance windows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the Private appliance (air-gapped) option: 

Summary of what I heard:
- You need an air-gapped appliance (on-prem, no egress) with private model runtime and local KV cache.
- Strict change windows for any firmware/software upgrades (monthly change window, scheduled by ProdOps).
- Preference for Redwood-managed image delivery vs customer-managed patching TBD.

Open questions to confirm (please fill out the attached site inventory template and share your network diagram):
1) Who will be the owner of appliance firmware/OS updates? (Options: Redwood-managed offline image + MOP, or GenoQuip-managed with Redwood-provided signed artifacts and checksums.)
2) What is your spare-parts policy? Do you expect Redwood to provide on-site spares or a swap-and-return RMA?
3) Can you confirm the physical custody model (locked rack + ProdOps-only access)?
4) Which change windows (day/time) do we need to target for any maintenance?

Preliminary Redwood guidance:
- Hardware baseline: 2x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent), dual NICs, TPM for key handling; we will produce a formal BOM once inventory is received.
- Upgrade model options:
  a) Managed offline upgrades: Redwood prepares signed images, ships encrypted USB bundle; ProdOps applies image during scheduled window using on-site MOP; Redwood validates post-upgrade logs during next business day.
  b) Customer-managed upgrades: GenoQuip pulls signed artifacts from a secure transfer (SFTP/airgap courier), runs the upgrade steps; Redwood provides the MOP and checksums and remote validation hooks (no egress required).

Attachments: site-inventory-template.csv (please populate) and a sample network-diagram.pdf (if available, share your actual diagram).

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the inventory template and send your network diagram (by EOD next Wed if possible).
- We run a focused technical workshop (1.5 hours) with ProdOps and your security lead to align on upgrade ownership and MOP. Proposed weeks: Nov 29 or Dec 6.
- Redwood to produce an initial BOM and two upgrade MOP drafts (managed vs customer-managed) after inventory is received.

If that all sounds right I can loop Ben (ops lead) to draft spare-part recommendations and a basic RMA flow.

Thanks — Irn

- For upgrades, our monthly maintenance window is the third Tuesday of each month, 00:00–03:00 local time.
- Spare parts: we expect a swap-and-return RMA (we do not keep spares on-site for vendor appliances). Please outline an RMA SLA (e.g., 48-hour swap).

I attached our high-level network diagram and will push the inventory template to our ProdOps queue.
